Class SlotNames

java.lang.Object
com.trevlar.menukit.api.window.SlotNames
public final class SlotNames extends Object
Display names for slots, on the client: labels like "Hotbar 3", "Chestplate" or "Offhand". Names are for display only and separate from identity (see Address).

Two sources, in priority order

  1. Per-address overrides (override(Address, String)): a name registered against a specific Address. MenuKit: Containers names its created slots this way when it creates them (group label and ordinal), and any consumer can name a custom slot. MenuKit never sees the created slot's type; the name is keyed by the address the consumer mints.
  2. Vanilla names, computed from the live slot's role. MenuKit already categorizes every vanilla slot through SlotGroupCategories (the 22 vanilla menus); naming is a table from each SlotGroupCategory to a SlotNames.Spec (a numbered label, or a list of single names), formatted with the slot's 1-based ordinal in its category. Nothing is stored for vanilla slots; the name is computed on each lookup.

Reads only

It reads SlotGroupCategories and the override map, and never touches Address, the window engine, the addressing or ContainerIdentity. Categories stay coarse: armor is still one PLAYER_ARMOR group for targeting, and the four names come from its SlotNames.Spec, not from splitting the category, which would change the category every panel-targeting consumer relies on.

Works with MenuKit alone: without Containers the override map is empty and vanilla names come from MenuKit's own resolvers. Lookups run on the client thread; the override map is concurrent because a created slot's name may be registered from another thread while the menu is built.
